entry.title: What happens to your muscles after months without gravity? 💪

media:group.media:title: What happens to your muscles after months without gravity? 💪
media:group.media:description:
Back on Earth, our astronaut Sophie Adenot took part in the Sarcolab experiment.
The experiment measures how spaceflight affects the muscles and tendons in the lower legs, helping scientists understand how the human body adapts to microgravity and recovers after returning to Earth.
Know someone who’d find this interesting? Share it with them! 📲
Sophie took part in these post-flight tests at :envihab, the @DLRde research facility in Cologne, Germany.
#ESA #Astronaut #Space

media:group.media:title: A dinosaur travelling through space? 🦖
media:group.media:description:
Back in August, we asked you to name the dinosaur sticker joining our Hera spacecraft on its journey. Now, more than 100 million kilometres from Earth, we finally have proof that our little passenger made it safely aboard!
The sticker is placed on Hera’s PALT baffle, which protects the laser altimeter from sunlight entering the instrument. 🛰️ But the adventure is far from over! On November 25, our little dino will reach the Didymos asteroid system to witness Hera investigate how asteroid deflection works.
Follow Chicxu’s journey and get the latest Hera insights, images and updates with the Hera Companion: 👉 hera.esa.int
##ESA #Asteroid #HeraMission

entry.title: 10 asteroid mysteries that ESA's Hera mission will explore

media:group.media:title: 10 asteroid mysteries that ESA's Hera mission will explore
media:group.media:description:
Hera, the European Space Agency’s first mission for planetary defence, arrives at its target body during November, with the goal of gathering precious data on the kinetic impact method of asteroid deflection – while also solving various scientific enigmas.
The small-car-sized spacecraft is headed to the 151-m-diameter Dimorphos asteroid, which orbits in turn around its 780-m Didymos parent. Dimorphos is already historic as the first object in the Solar System to have had its orbit changed by human action – when NASA’s DART spacecraft impacted it on 26 September 2022.
DART’s impact caused a brightening visible from distant Earth telescopes, but nobody knows what it did to Dimorphos itself. Hera is going there to perform a close-up crash site survey, to help turn DART’s kinetic impact experiment into a well understood planetary defence deflection technique.
Scientists are hoping for bonus science as well. Past spacecraft close encounters have revealed asteroids to be dynamic environments with complex histories – and many outstanding questions still to be answered. Here are 10 asteroid mysteries that Hera will explore.
Read more: https://www.esa.int/Space_Safety/Hera/10_asteroid_mysteries_Hera_will_explore
Credits: European Space Agency (ESA)

entry.title: What’s life like at one of the most isolated research stations on Earth? ❄️👀

media:group.media:title: What’s life like at one of the most isolated research stations on Earth? ❄️👀
media:group.media:description:
Welcome to Concordia Station in Antarctica, around 1,200 km inland and more than 3,000 metres above sea level. For nine months of the year, the station is inaccessible, even in an emergency. Its harsh surroundings have earned it the nickname “White Mars”.
Our medical doctor Sarah Gaier takes us on a tour, showing us some of the unusual things that make perfect sense when you live and work in such an extreme environment.
Could you live somewhere this remote? Send this to the person you’d take with you 🥶
#ESA #Space #Antarctica

entry.title: Those two tiny dots? They are asteroids 👀☄️

media:group.media:title: Those two tiny dots? They are asteroids 👀☄️
media:group.media:description:
For the first time, Hera has seen Didymos and Dimorphos as two separate asteroids. From 1,280 km away, tiny Dimorphos appears as just around one pixel.
But not for long! Hera will get a much closer look in November, investigating the aftermath of NASA’s DART impact and helping us learn more about planetary defence.
Got questions about Hera, DART or the asteroids? Ask the Hera Space Companion 👉 hera.esa.int
#ESA #Satellite #HeraMission

entry.title: What happened this month at the European Space Agency? (October 2026)

media:group.media:title: What happened this month at the European Space Agency? (October 2026)
media:group.media:description:
October was a month of discoveries and milestones. ESA’s Rosalind Franklin rover team trained in Spain’s desert, preparing for Mars. Our Smile mission captured the full ring of northern lights around Earth, while Mars Express uncovered new clues about a giant Martian cloud. ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot returned to Earth after 237 days in space, and Hera captured its first images of the asteroids it will study to help protect our planet. Meanwhile, ESA welcomed thousands of visitors for Open Days and teamed up with Pokémon to bring space science to new audiences.
Here’s a look at what space had in store for Europe this October.

entry.title: Two mannequins flew around the Moon, and only one wore a vest 🌙

media:group.media:title: Two mannequins flew around the Moon, and only one wore a vest 🌙
media:group.media:description:
Helga and Zohar flew on Artemis I in 2022 to measure radiation beyond Earth’s protection. Helga went without a vest, while Zohar wore the AstroRad vest.
Now we know what a difference it could make. In a strong solar storm like the one in August 1972, the vest could cut an astronaut’s radiation dose by almost 60%.
#ESA #Artemis #SpaceRadiation

entry.title: What makes our experts dedicate their work lives to asteroids? 🪨🛰️

media:group.media:title: What makes our experts dedicate their work lives to asteroids? 🪨🛰️
media:group.media:description:
For some, it starts with a childhood fascination. For others, it’s the thrill of exploring the unknown. Our Hera engineers tell us what keeps them fascinated by these cosmic neighbours.
In November, Hera will finally reach the Didymos asteroid system to investigate the aftermath of NASA’s DART mission, which intentionally impacted Didymos’ moon, Dimorphos, in 2022 to test whether humanity could deflect an asteroid threatening Earth.
While the first close-up images of Didymos are expected earlier in the month, 25 November marks a particularly special moment: the first close-up look at Dimorphos.
After years of preparing for this moment, even Ian and Ingo can’t wait to discover what’s waiting out there. How do you think it will look like? 👀
#ESA #Satellite #HeraMission

entry.title: Finding Our Way: Inside the Galileo Project (ESA documentary)

media:group.media:title: Finding Our Way: Inside the Galileo Project (ESA documentary)
media:group.media:description:
Finding Our Way: Inside the Galileo Project takes viewers inside one of Europe’s most ambitious technological endeavours: the creation and operation of Galileo, Europe’s global navigation satellite system. Born from a vision of independence and innovation, Galileo reflects decades of determination to secure Europe’s autonomous access to precise positioning, navigation and timing. Discover the story behind the signal that guides us all.
